title: He Was Shot for Voting.

brand.cta: Follow The Black History Room for one story a day.

beats.text: Born free in Charleston in 1839, he grew up in Philadelphia and graduated top of his class.
He became a teacher, and in the Civil War he recruited Black regiments.
In 1865, he refused to leave a whites-only streetcar. They left him sitting in it all night.
In 1867, Pennsylvania outlawed segregation on its streetcars. His campaign forced it.
He co-founded a Black baseball club. In 1867, the national association voted them out.
In 1870, the Fifteenth Amendment gave Black men the vote.
On Election Day, October 10, 1871, white mobs attacked Black voters in Philadelphia.
On his way to vote, a man named Frank Kelly shot him dead. He was 32.

visual.caption: Octavius V. Catto, engraving after a photograph, 1871

beats.text: Kelly was tried in 1877. An all-white jury set him free.
In 2017, Philadelphia raised a statue of him at City Hall. Its first of a Black American.

facts.claim: Born free, Charleston SC, 22 Feb 1839; Institute for Colored Youth, Philadelphia; graduated 1858 (valedictorian per NPS).
Taught at the ICY; recruited Black soldiers in the Civil War; slogan 'Men of color to arms! Now or never!' (SABR).
18 May 1865: refused to leave a streetcar and was left sitting in it overnight.
March 1867 Pennsylvania law barring removal of passengers by colour; Catto's campaign / 'bill of rights' behind it.
Co-founded the Pythian Base Ball Club (1866/67); 1867 the National Association of Base Ball Players denied them membership, formalising a colour line.
Fifteenth Amendment ratified 1870; Catto a persistent advocate.
Election Day 10 Oct 1871: violence against Black voters in Philadelphia; police did little to intervene.
Shot by Frank Kelly near his home on South Street, aged 32.
Funeral among the largest in the city's history; Kelly tried April 1877 and acquitted by a jury with no African Americans.
Memorial 'A Quest for Parity' with a 12-foot bronze statue unveiled at City Hall, 26 Sept 2017; first public statue of an individual African American in Philadelphia.
